info.name: Payroll Run — Continuous Flow & Maker-Checker
info.description:
The payroll module as **one resumable flow** with maker-checker approval.

**Base URL:** `{{base_url}}/api/companies/{{company_id}}/payroll-runs`

---

### The flow

```
setup → generate → adjust → review → approval → payment → payslips → done
        └────────── MAKER ──────────┘ └──── CHECKER ────┘ └─ MAKER ─┘
```

A **payroll run** owns the whole journey. It carries `current_step` and `status`, and every transition is validated and written to an audit trail (`payroll_run_events`).

### Resuming

`GET /resume` is the entry point. A user who walks away mid-flow is dropped back exactly where they left off — never track the step client-side.

### Maker-checker

Whoever prepared a run **cannot approve it** (`403`). Submitting locks the run for edits so an approval always describes what actually gets paid. Rejection needs a reason and re-opens the run at `adjust`.

Waivable per company via `allow_self_approval` / `require_approval` in payroll settings.

### Run statuses

| Status | Editable by maker | Checker action |
|---|---|---|
| `draft` / `in_progress` | ✅ | — |
| `pending_approval` | ❌ locked | Approve / Reject |
| `rejected` | ✅ re-opened | — |
| `approved` | ❌ | Pay |
| `paid` | payslips only | Complete |
| `completed` / `cancelled` | ❌ terminal | — |

### Roles
- `isManager` (Admin **or** Manager) — maker actions
- `isAdmin` — checker actions, and settings

Every response is `{ success, message, data }`. On failure, `message` is written to be shown to an end user verbatim.

request.description:
**Role:** `isManager` (Admin or Manager)

**Call this first, on every payroll page load.**

Returns every run that is neither `completed` nor `cancelled`, plus `active_run` — the one the UI should open by default (most recent period first).

This is what makes the flow resumable: a user who closed the tab halfway through Adjustments comes back to exactly that step. Never store the current step client-side; `progress.current_step` here is the truth.

Optional `?branch_id=` narrows to one branch.

request.description:
**Role:** `isManager`

Opens a payroll run. Pass **either** `payroll_period_id` (use an existing period) **or** `period_name` + `start_date` + `end_date` (create one inline) — so 'new payroll' is a single call rather than create-period-then-go-find-it.

`branch_id: null` runs the whole company.

**If a live run already exists for that period + branch, this returns `200` with `resumed: true` and hands back the existing run.** That is a success, not a conflict — open it.

The run starts at `status: in_progress`, `current_step: generate`.

request.description:
**Role:** `isManager`

Computes every active employee's salary for the period and freezes a day-by-day snapshot into `payroll_daily_lines`.

Runs inside **one transaction** — either every employee lands or none do.

`force: true` regenerates employees who already have a payroll for this period. Regeneration happens **in place**, so manual adjustments keyed to the payroll survive and are re-applied to the fresh base. Already-`paid` and `cancelled` payrolls are never touched.

Employees with no active salary structure are **skipped, not failed** — they come back in `skipped[]` so the UI can link straight to the fix.

request.description:
**Role:** `isAdmin`

**Salary calculation**
- `per_day_basis` — `calendar_days` (gross ÷ days in period; week-offs are paid) · `fixed_30` (gross ÷ 30; Gulf/KSA convention) · `working_days` (gross ÷ non-week-off, non-holiday days)
- `half_day_leave_is_payable` — a paid half-day leave is half leave + half worked, so the day is fully payable
- `prorate_joiners_leavers` — days before `joining_date` / after `exit_date` become `not_employed` rather than absence
- `overtime_on_off_days` — pay overtime for hours worked on a week-off or holiday

**Sandwich leave** — the group people get wrong
- `sandwich_enabled` — turn the rule off entirely
- `sandwich_applies_to` — which off-days may be bridged. Most policies are `week_off` only
- `sandwich_requires_full_day` — **keep this `true`**. Only a full day of lost pay on *both* sides triggers a sandwich. With it `false`, a half day either side of a weekend makes that weekend unpaid
- `sandwich_max_bridge_days` — longest stretch that can be swallowed, so one absence either side of a long shutdown cannot zero out the whole thing

**Approvals**
- `require_approval` — `false` makes submitting auto-approve
- `allow_self_approval` — `true` waives the maker-checker rule
- `auto_email_payslips` — default for the payment dialog's email checkbox

Changes apply to the **next** payroll generation. Existing runs keep their frozen figures.
